attachment_scope.A1_left_rule: published qualitative group order plus deterministic normalized lanes
attachment_scope.right_rule: exact theta mirror of the A1-left hypothesis

topology.description: The frozen axial-steering neural path drives existing named fibers. For each mirrored non-transverse A1-A3 identity pair, only active tension above the weaker side replaces its previous axial proxy with a full 3D attachment-line force. The equal-activation axial baseline is unchanged. No yaw or curvature target enters the body.

connections.edge: bilateral field samples -> sensory and anterior motor path
connections.allowed_use: reuse of the frozen Stage 9 neural path only

connections.edge: A1 muscle identity -> normalized attachment line
connections.evidence: Zarin et al., eLife 2019, doi:10.7554/eLife.51781; Carayon et al., eLife 2020, doi:10.7554/eLife.57547
connections.allowed_use: qualitative topology and deterministic normalized attachment hypothesis only

connections.edge: A1 attachment hypothesis -> right side and A2-A3
connections.allowed_use: bilateral mirror and segment homology; not measured coordinates
engineering calibration in model units only

limitations: This is not a reconstructed complete L1 steering connectome.
The attachment coordinates are normalized ANATOMY_DERIVED hypotheses, not digitized or measured L1 attachment coordinates.
A2-A3 reuse A1 attachment homology and the right side is an exact mirror; missing individual variation is not claimed.
No individual CSA, force gain, or force in newtons is available; all tension and force values are MODEL_FITTED model units.
The reduced centerline body receives the attachment-line force as equivalent shared-node forces and reports the resulting moment; it does not resolve cuticle cross-section deformation.
Transverse identities remain in contact-release control and are excluded from the spatial steering force.
The field is a generic bounded scalar and does not identify attraction, aversion, or a specific receptor modality. Gradient sign is not a behavioral preference claim.
L2 pivot evidence constrains relative anterior support only and is not copied as an L1 absolute amplitude.

parameter_provenance.objective: Preserve the frozen uniform axial trajectory exactly while mirrored field gradients produce bounded, mirrored, distributed anterior deformation through named attachment forces without an active-curvature constraint.
parameter_provenance.uncertainty: The scale is not a measured L1 muscle force, stress, moment arm, CSA, Fmax, stiffness, or damping value.

mechanics.replacement_rule: subtract the stronger-side active-tension excess from the existing local-tangent proxy, then add the same named fiber's full attachment-line force at the fitted spatial scale

required_gates: uniform field is exactly the frozen axial-v1 trajectory and executes no attachment-excess force
opposite gradients generate mirrored heading, position, attachment moment, and T3-A3 planar bend
every attachment force has an earlier field, sensory, premotor, motor-neuron, and muscle-activation trace
equal-and-opposite attachment force has only numerical net-force residual
sensory and motor lesions attenuate the corresponding response; attachment lesion preserves upstream activity but removes spatial force
active curvature, yaw input, behavior command, FSM, policy, and authored translation never execute
forward progress, segment extension, chord ratio, local bend, and lateral slip stay within rejection gates
validation.claim_limit: Connectome-driven embodied steering research approximation with anatomy-derived normalized attachment lines and model-fitted force scale; not measured L1 attachment mechanics or independently validated biological steering.
